# Extension catalog

Pick the agent whose line matches the work and dispatch it. You see agents, not their skills: each worker launches with core plus only its own extension and finds that extension's skills through the extension's router.

## Agents

| Agent | What it does, when to dispatch | Claude Code |
|---|---|---|
| `george-coding-agent:coding` | Coding worker that builds or fixes code one verified slice at a time. Dispatch when: implement, fix, refactor, test or build work in a code repo. | `claude --agent george-coding-agent:coding` |
| `george-coding-agent:reviewer` | Fresh-context read-only reviewer that grades a diff, doc or plan against its contract and a checklist. Dispatch when: a diff, doc or plan needs an adversarial review. | `claude --agent george-coding-agent:reviewer` |

From a home, launch with `bin/fm-spawn.sh ... --agent <plugin>:<agent>`: the spawn turns on core and that one extension for the worker and turns every other known extension off. By hand: `claude --agent <plugin>:<agent> --settings "$(bin/jarvis-plugins-for.sh <plugin>)"`. Codex has no agent files and no per-launch plugin switch: start the worker with a brief whose first line is "Load `$role-<agent>` first" (docs/jarvis-plugins.md, "Skill listing budget"). Other tools: tell the worker to load `role-<agent>`.

## Installed or not

Check before routing. Claude Code: `claude plugin list` shows `<plugin>@jarvis-ai-george` or `<plugin>@<plugin>` (installed from its own marketplace); either counts, enabled or not. Codex: its plugin list, under either marketplace. In a home, `bin/jarvis-setup.sh status` checks the current tool.

When the work needs an agent whose extension is not installed, ask in one line, for example "That needs the coding agent from GeorgeCodingAgent. Install it?" On yes, run its install line yourself, then dispatch; the manager needs no restart. Never install without that yes.

| Extension | Install (Claude Code) | Install (Codex) |
|---|---|---|
| GeorgeCodingAgent | `claude plugin install george-coding-agent@jarvis-ai-george` | `codex plugin add george-coding-agent@jarvis-ai-george` (after `codex plugin marketplace add georgewangyu/JarvisAIGeorge`) |

## Core skills

To use a skill, load it with the Skill tool when it is in your skill list, else read its file: `../<skill>/SKILL.md`, relative to this skill's folder (its base directory). Follow that file as if it had been invoked. Skills marked "no" are hidden from the skill list to keep the list inside its budget; they are not deprecated.

| Skill | What it is for | Listed |
|---|---|---|
| [`brainstorm`](../brainstorm/SKILL.md) | Turn a rough idea or an open "how should we do X" into a decision: ground in the code, challenge premises, compare a few real options, and recommend one. | yes |
| [`grill-me`](../grill-me/SKILL.md) | Interview the user until the intent or every decision in a plan is settled, one question at a time with a recommended answer. | yes |
| [`mistake-miner`](../mistake-miner/SKILL.md) | Collect agent mistakes into an append-only inbox, then cluster repeats weekly so a human picks a lasting fix (a check, a rule, a test). | no |
| [`principles`](../principles/SKILL.md) | Index of the principle skills for judging a claim, a number, a design, or agent scaffolding. | no |
| [`principles-bitter-lesson`](../principles-bitter-lesson/SKILL.md) | Judge whether agent scaffolding (a skill, rule, prompt, hook or eval) will compound or decay as models improve. | no |
| [`principles-first-principles`](../principles-first-principles/SKILL.md) | Check a number or a design from fundamentals with a back-of-envelope bound (cores, bandwidth, latency, queueing). | no |
| [`principles-scientific-method`](../principles-scientific-method/SKILL.md) | Test a claim like a scientist: a falsifiable hypothesis, a prediction before acting, one change at a time against a baseline, and a confidence label. | no |
| [`role-jarvis`](../role-jarvis/SKILL.md) | Act as the `jarvis-ai-george` role (for tools without agent files). | no |
